--- note
Promoted from matrix cell tex/nested-bf-em/mid/w80/desktop (FINDINGS.md #5, rule R-V5).
A vertical landing that falls inside the merged hidden prefix run of a nested command (\textbf{\emph{) must settle on the first genuinely visible argument character.
The one-shot snap parked the caret between the two hidden prefixes (the outer argument start IS the inner \emph{'s own prefix) and both commands popped open; the snap now iterates to a fixpoint.
WebKit's moveVertically lands mid-prefix routinely while chromium's raw landing tends to resolve to the boundary already, so the webkit lanes are the ones this fixture bites on.
